# Certified composition from coarse survival observations

29 October 2026, Brisbane. This construction preserves hidden source memory,
uses fresh common preparations and live/absorbed reports, and certifies every
fixed switching word. Its executed source has countably infinitely many
states, norm one and infinite mean lifetime. A two-state approximation is
certified without assuming finite hidden rank.

The ingredients are established: positive-operator domination, weak Poincare
inequalities, energy estimates, confidence intervals, prefix trees and moment
realization. The useful contract joins finite native lifetime acquisition,
simultaneous switching-tail control, paid mixed-word observations, and finite
verification of a model's every-word output. Historical priority and generic
efficient learning are not established.

## Common preparation and the observable energy inequality

Let A_i be positivity-preserving selfadjoint contractions sharing a positive
unit vector v with A_i v<=v. On countable coordinates, mu_j=v_j^2 is a
probability distribution and P_i(j,k)=A_i(j,k)v_k/v_j is a substochastic
kernel reversible for mu. Prepare mu and report only live/absorbed. The
survival of a chronological word is f(w)=<v,A_wv>. Reversal preserves this
scalar. Every reachable x=A_wv satisfies 0<=x<=v.

The common reversible preparation is a structural access premise. Selfdual
readout alone does not establish the order condition. No boundary identity,
hidden dimension, strict source norm cap or uncensored lifetime bound is
supplied. A surviving coarse label never silently resets the actual source.

For any integer m>=1, the spectral inequality
1-lambda^(2m)<=m(1-lambda^2), |lambda|<=1, and order domination imply

    ||x||^2 <= m E_i(x)+f(i^(2m))||x/v||_infinity^2,
    E_i(x)=||x||^2-||A_i x||^2.                         (1)

Indeed, |A_i^m x|<=||x/v||_infinity A_i^m v. Equality at x=v proves

    sup_(|x|<=v) ||A_i^m x||^2 = ||A_i^m v||^2=f(i^(2m)).

Thus one accessible scalar supplies a uniform coefficient on the relevant
order interval. If simultaneous observations give s>=max_i f(i^(2m)),
then every switched state of length h satisfies

    ||A_wv||^2 <= z_h=s+(1-1/m)^h(1-s).                 (2)

Apply (1) at the selected action and iterate. Splitting a word into lengths
a,b and using reversal and Cauchy-Schwarz gives f(w)<=sqrt(z_a z_b).

# Independent review of the paid coarse switching cover

## Verdict and exact scope

The acquisition, selected-prefix statistics, finite-cover certificate and complete resource ledger in `core/coarse_switching_cover.py` pass this scoped review. The finite tree gives an absolute survival error at most 1/16 for every switching word on its simultaneous confidence event. It uses chosen controls, fresh preparations and coarse alive/absorbed reports; no microscopic state label is supplied to inference.

An independent replay verified the 168 confidence endpoints used by the selected 84 nodes, all 32 pure-curve upper endpoints, every potential-prefix denominator and count partition, finite-tree completeness and the exact resource totals. It generated **no trajectories**. The general weak-Poincare implication from pure repetition curves to switching tails is assigned to the scalar branch; this review checks its saved statistical inputs and recurrence arithmetic, not that general lemma.

## Why balanced prefix counts are binomial

The control design is fixed before the corresponding trajectories: each of the 2^10 length-10 binary tapes receives 512 independent fresh preparations. Consequently each fixed length-h prefix w has exactly

\[
N_w=512\,2^{10-h}=524288/2^h
\]

assigned trials. The initial hidden-state distribution is identical for all tapes. Assignment does not inspect the prepared microstate or slow level.

For every assigned trial, the first h controls are exactly w. Under causal dynamics, the future tape suffix cannot affect survival through that prefix. Thus the survival indicators for this fixed prefix are independent Bernoulli variables with common mean f(w), and their sum is binomial with denominator N_w.

The denominator is **all assigned trials**, not the number alive at the parent. A trajectory that died earlier contributes zero to each longer prefix on its already assigned tape. The implementation obtains the same unconditional count by grouping the remaining active trajectories while retaining N_w as the denominator. It never refreshes a hidden state after a coarse live report.

# Scoped review of the certified two-state coarse model

## Verdict

The new use of the accepted confidence cover in `core/coarse_compressed_model.py` is sound. The saved rational two-state candidate is a valid positive substochastic model, and its 84 deterministic checks certify every finite switching word from the declared preparation at absolute survival error at most

\[
15583954301/250000000000=0.062335817204.
\]

The maximum error bound at retained branch words is approximately 0.01676534263. This is a certificate for a finite approximation to the scalar response, not a claim that the physical source has two states or finite hidden rank.

This review checked only the new implication, exact candidate admissibility and saved node bounds. It did not repeat the accepted cover statistics, source acquisition, trajectory work or weak-Poincare review. No source queries or trajectories were generated.

## The cover-to-model implication

Let f(w) be the true survival response and g(w) the candidate's total survival after the same word. Condition on the already accepted simultaneous event that f(v) lies in the saved interval [l_v,u_v] for every selected node v. This event holds uniformly before selecting the fitted candidate.

If a word ends at a branch node v, then

\[
|f(v)-g(v)|\le\max\{|l_v-g(v)|,|u_v-g(v)|\}.
\]

If a word extends a terminal prefix v, write it as vs. Irreversible absorption gives 0≤f(vs)≤f(v)≤u_v. Candidate substochasticity gives 0≤g(vs)≤g(v). Therefore

\[
|f(vs)-g(vs)|\le\max\{u_v,g(v)\}.
\]

The larger of the two prefix survival uppers is sufficient; adding them would be unnecessarily loose. The accepted finite tree guarantees that every nonempty word either ends at a retained branch or extends a terminal prefix. The empty word is exactly one under both preparations. Taking the maximum of these finitely many bounds proves the all-word result.

The candidate may be chosen using the same observed data. On the simultaneous interval event, the displayed inequalities hold for **every** admissible candidate that passes their deterministic checks. Consequently fitting the proposal to early moments consumes no new confidence budget and needs no independent validation batch. The float-based moment calculation and rounding propose a rational candidate; they do not establish its validity or substitute for the exact final checks.
